evals.name: dns-cutover-no-agent-access
evals.prompt: we're moving the marketing site off the old droplet onto vercel this thursday. our dns is in cloudflare but only our ops lead has the login, and i can get him on a call for about 20 minutes, that's it. can you write me something i can literally read to him line by line? right now there's an A record for www.brightlane.io pointing at 143.198.72.14, and it needs to become a CNAME to cname.vercel-dns.com. i'm nervous about this because last time someone did a cutover we had the site down for three hours and nobody could tell whether it was propagation or just a wrong record.
evals.expected_output: A runbook the user can read aloud. Should settle the boundary, capture the current record before it is overwritten, give an exact click path plus reasoned do-nots, separate the apply action from propagation delay, and self-check in a second channel (a resolver, not the Cloudflare UI). Should not present the user-supplied IP as a measured baseline.
assertions: States that the agent has no access to the Cloudflare account and that the ops lead performs every change
Instructs capturing or screenshotting the existing A record BEFORE it is overwritten, because the change destroys the old value
Gives a concrete navigation path inside Cloudflare rather than a vague description of where to look
Every 'do not' item carries the reason for the prohibition
Separates the save/apply action from DNS propagation delay, and says which one explains a stale answer
The self-check reads a resolver (dig, nslookup, or an external DNS checker) rather than re-reading the Cloudflare UI
Labels the 143.198.72.14 baseline as user-supplied and unverified, rather than stating it as a measured fact
Tells the ops lead a rollback action (restore the A record) and what would trigger it

evals.name: rds-parameter-pending-reboot
evals.prompt: i need to turn on slow query logging on our production postgres in RDS - set log_min_duration_statement to 500ms. i'm the only one with AWS console access so i have to click it myself, but you can read the database directly, there's a read-only user in .env. can you walk me through it and then confirm it actually took effect? i've been burned before where i changed a parameter group and nothing happened.
evals.expected_output: Baseline read from the DB before the console steps, target stated as an assertion, console click path, explicit handling of the saved-vs-in-effect gap, and a SQL self-check.
assertions: Reads (or states it will read) the current parameter value from the database BEFORE giving the console steps
States the expected after-value as an explicit assertion before the user acts
Addresses the saved-but-not-in-effect gap for RDS parameter groups, including whether a reboot or apply is required
The self-check is a SQL read the user can run alone (SHOW, current_setting, or pg_settings)
Verification happens in a channel different from the AWS console where the change was made
Says plainly that it could not reach the live database, rather than presenting an invented current value
The apply/save action appears as its own numbered step, not as a clause inside another step
Warns that the parameter group may be shared by more than one instance, or otherwise names what must not change

evals.name: intercom-property-partial-removal
evals.prompt: we're deprecating a custom contact property called legacy_tier in our intercom workspace. when i search for it it shows up in something like 40 places but i'm pretty sure most of those are just references rather than things i actually have to touch. i need it off the contact sidebar and out of any saved segments that filter on it, but absolutely NOT deleted from the underlying data - finance still exports it. i'll do all the clicking, you tell me what to click and then check i did it right.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to build the runbook off the '40 places' figure, separates raw matches from actionable objects, carries the do-not-delete near-miss, splits into verified steps, and gives a self-check.
assertions: Does not accept the user's '40 places' figure as the work list, and explicitly separates raw search matches from objects the user must actually click
States that the property and its stored data must NOT be deleted, and names that as the dangerous adjacent action
Splits the sidebar work and the segment work into separate steps with a verification point between them
Declares what must not change (a blast-radius assertion) in addition to the success condition
Provides a self-check the user can run without the agent
States that it cannot read the workspace and asks the user (or a read-only API call) to supply the real counts, instead of inventing them
Warns that removing the property from a saved segment can change that segment's membership, or otherwise flags a side effect on dependent objects
